import torch
import torch as t

def solve(rows):
    """Return (a.T in order?, copy in order?, same values?, own block?)."""
    a = t.tensor(rows)
    view = a.T
    packed = view.contiguous()
    return (view.is_contiguous(), packed.is_contiguous(),
            t.equal(packed, view), packed.data_ptr() != a.data_ptr())


example = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]
print(solve(example))

wrong_examples.why: `.contiguous()` returns a NEW tensor with its own block, in reading order. Reusing the view leaves three of the four answers wrong.
